Your class is your hero's calling. It's not a job, it's who you are when the torches gutter and the door slams shut behind you. Nine classes. Nine ways to face the darkness. Pick the one that makes you grin.

#callout(type: "note", title: "Classes Shape Costs, Not Limits", body: [
Your class gives you a Discipline, a signature ability, and cheaper access to certain skills and Disciplines. It does not restrict what you can buy, only what comes easily. A Protector who studies Arcana pays more for it. That's the point. Be unusual, just know it'll cost you.
])

== The Protector

_"Stand behind me."_

The Protector stands at the vanguard, using body and armor as a shield for those in their care. You are the anchor, built on Brawn and Fortitude, trained to absorb blows that would fell lesser heroes. Your pride is not in the enemies you slay but in the allies who walk away unharmed because you stood in the gap. You pursue ever-better ways to fortify your resilience while keeping the ability to strike back when needed.

*Class Discipline (L1):* Armor (1) + 1 any Weapon

*Signature, Bastion:* Spend your movement to enter a defensive stance. Add +1 to your Protection Value for the round.

*Favored Skills:* Athletics, Endurance, Survival, Perception, Persuasion, Medicine

*Starting Kit:* Battleaxe, chain mail (DR 5), shield (+2 DR), smith's tools, 10 gp.

*Discipline Costs (Rank 1 / Rank 2 / Rank 3):*

== The Blade

_"Strike once. Strike true. Strike last."_

The Blade masters the art of finesse and precision, favoring the swift elegance of light blades. Your expertise lies in meticulously placed stabs, exploiting vulnerabilities with the sharpness and agility of your weapons. Keyed to Guile, you weave through the battlefield, striking with calculated precision, each strike as effective as it is lethal. You are the shadow on the wall, the final face your enemies see.

*Class Discipline (L1):* Blades (1) + Stealth (1)

*Signature, Swift Blade:* You may use Agility instead of Brawn when attacking with blades. When you exploit an opening (a target that is Dazed, Prone, or unaware of you), the attack deals +1 damage tier. Once per scene.

*Favored Skills:* Acrobatics, Deception, Perception, Sleight of Hand, Stealth, Thievery

*Starting Kit:* Shortsword, dagger, leather armor (DR 2), thieves' tools, 15 gp.

*Discipline Costs (Rank 1 / Rank 2 / Rank 3):*

== The Arcanist

_"Fire answers to me."_

The Arcanist delves into the mysteries of arcane energies, mastering their manipulation to bend the fabric of reality. Your focus is harnessing these powerful forces, channeling them into spells that devastate foes and alter the course of battle. Keyed to Knowledge, you weave complex incantations with deep understanding, summoning energies that shimmer with potential. Every spell fires. Every single one. The question is never _if_, only how well.

*Class Discipline (L1):* Energy (1) + Fire (1)

*Signature, Arcane Shield:* As a free action, raise a protective ward that gives +1 to your Protection Value for the round. Once per round.

*Favored Skills:* Alchemy, Arcana, History, Lore, Nature

*Starting Kit:* Arcane focus, dagger, scholar's robes (DR 0), focus pouch, spellbook, 5 gp.

*Discipline Costs (Rank 1 / Rank 2 / Rank 3):*

There are no spell slots. No mana. No "I'm out of spells." Your magic always goes off. Weak hit? The spell still fires, just not as hard. This changes everything about playing a caster. You're never useless. You're never out of options.
])

== The Shepherd

_"The light guides my hand."_

The Shepherd stands as a beacon of guidance, providing moral direction and harnessing divine energies to aid allies. Your path is one of enlightenment, using a deep connection to the divine to inspire and protect those around you. Through word and deed, you channel power into abilities that heal, shield, and uplift your companions. Keyed to Reason, your wisdom discerns the right course in the murkiest of situations, offering light in darkness. You also stand as a bulwark against the undead, creatures that have slipped beyond death's reach fear your presence.

*Class Discipline (L1):* Protection (1) + Animal (1)

*Signature, Unholy Word:* Call down divine energy that ignores armor and affects only undead creatures within your presence. Your faith burns what should not walk.

*Favored Skills:* Medicine, Nature, Religion, Survival

*Starting Kit:* Shortsword, holy symbol, leather armor (DR 2), healer's kit, 5 gp.

*Discipline Costs (Rank 1 / Rank 2 / Rank 3):*

Healing in Heroes of Legend is precious. HP recovery is slow outside of magic. A Shepherd in the party changes the calculus of every fight. Your allies will love you. The DA will have to work harder to threaten them.
])

== The Intellect

_"I've read about this."_

The Intellect embodies cerebral prowess and scholarly mastery. Your path is a relentless pursuit of knowledge, delving into ancient tomes, unlocking the mysteries of the universe. With a mind as sharp as a finely honed blade, you navigate the world through logic and reason. Keyed to Knowledge, you are not defined by brute strength but by cunning and foresight. Through tactical acumen and strategic planning, you outmaneuver foes with calculated precision, turning their own weaknesses against them. Your words carry weight, guiding allies through the darkest times.

*Class Discipline (L1):* Any one (1) + Lore (1)

*Signature, Knowledge Is Power:* Gain +1 to all Knowledge-based skill checks.

*Favored Skills:* History, Lore, Medicine, Arcana, Perception

*Starting Kit:* Shortsword, spellbook, scholar's robes (DR 0), focus pouch, ink & pen, 10 gp.

*Discipline Costs (Rank 1 / Rank 2 / Rank 3):*

== The Odd

_"I have a trick for that."_

The Odd embodies eccentricity and peculiarity. With a demeanor that dances on the edge of madness and a style that defies convention, you bring chaos and unpredictability to every encounter. Keyed to Guile, your appearance is striking: mismatched clothing, bizarre accessories, an unusual hairstyle. In battle, you are a whirlwind of unorthodox tactics: spells with unconventional gestures, bizarre weapons wielded with deadly precision, strange powers that defy explanation. Your adversaries never know what to expect. Sometimes, neither do you.

*Class Discipline (L1):* Any one, different category (1) + 1 any, different category.

*Signature, Eccentric Spellcasting:* Choose one arcane ability and one divine ability. You ignore prerequisite Disciplines for these two (level requirements still apply). You need no arcane focus or holy symbol.

*Favored Skills:* Sleight of Hand, Stealth, Deception, Acrobatics, Performance

*Starting Kit:* Shortbow, dagger, leather armor (DR 2), thieves' tools, 20 arrows.

*Discipline Costs (Rank 1 / Rank 2 / Rank 3):*

Odd has no Home disciplines: every discipline costs 2/4/8 (Adjacent).

== The Leader

_"Together, we are unstoppable."_

The Leader is a beacon of courage on the battlefield, leading from the front lines with valor and resolve. Keyed to Reason, your stirring speeches and tactical acumen rally allies to action, instilling confidence even in the face of adversity. Beyond command, you serve as mentor and confidant, recognizing and nurturing the potential within each member of your group. Driven by a clear vision and unwavering commitment, you guide your companions toward a brighter future. In your presence, unity flourishes.

*Class Discipline (L1):* Tactics (1) + Protection (1)

*Signature, Lead by Example:* When you land a telling blow on an enemy, grant one ally who witnessed it a +2 bonus on their next roll. Your actions inspire greatness in others.

*Favored Skills:* Persuasion, Perception, Insight, Survival, Endurance

*Starting Kit:* Longsword, spear, leather armor (DR 2), shield (+2 DR), 10 gp.

*Discipline Costs (Rank 1 / Rank 2 / Rank 3):*

== The Unbalanced

_"Power has a price. I'm willing to pay."_

The Unbalanced is a wild card, embodying chaos and unpredictability in every action. Your demeanor is marked by erratic energy, veering between bouts of laughter and brooding intensity. Behind your unpredictable facade lies a mind that operates on its own unique wavelength, calculating the odds even as you appear to embrace madness. In battle, you unleash pent-up frenzy with ferocious abandon, your fighting style, as unpredictable as your personality. You thrive on the chaos of combat, reveling in the uncertainty of the fray.

*Class Discipline (L1):* Any Elemental (1) + 1 opposing Elemental (1)

*Signature, Edge of Chaos:* On a Strong hit, deal +1 damage tier (one row up on the damage budget) but roll on the d6 Backlash Table below.

*Backlash Table (d6):*

#figure(
  align(center)[#table(
    columns: (33.33%, 66.67%),
    align: (auto, auto,),
    table.header([d6], [Result]),
    [1], [You take 4 damage.],
    [2], [Your next attack roll is at Bane.],
    [3], [You lose your Maneuver this turn.],
    [4], [The backlash lashes out: an adjacent enemy takes 2 damage of the spell's type.],
    [5], [You take 2 damage; the target takes +2.],
    [6], [Wild surge: the DA picks a minor random effect (a cantrip fires, a small object ignites, etc.).],
  )],
  kind: table,
  outlined: false,
  numbering: none,
)

*Favored Skills:* Arcana, Deception, Insight, Perception, Acrobatics

*Starting Kit:* Spear, focus pouch, scholar's robes (DR 0), six vials of volatile reagents, 5 gp.

*Discipline Costs (Rank 1 / Rank 2 / Rank 3):*

Choose two opposing Elemental Disciplines at Level 1 (Fire/Water or Earth/Wind). Those become Home. The other two elements become Opposed. Animal, Plants, and Energy are Home (1/2/4); Life and Summon are Adjacent (2/4/8); Religion and Mind are Foreign (3/6/12).

#callout(type: "note", title: "Embrace the Chaos", body: [
You're not broken. You're balanced on a knife's edge between opposing forces, and that tension is your source of power. When it works, you're the most dangerous person in the room. When it doesn't, well, that's entertaining too. The party keeps you around because when everything goes wrong, you're the one who knows what to do with wrong.
])

== The Shadow

_"You never saw me."_

The Shadow is the ghost in the room, the whisper no one heard, the hand that lifts a key from a guard's belt while the guard is still wearing it. Where the Blade wins by stabbing first, the Shadow wins by never being seen at all. You are keyed to Agility and Guile in equal measure, a creature of silence and misdirection. Doors open for you. Traps disarm themselves at your touch. Identities are costumes you wear and discard. Your fighting style is dirty, fast, and never, ever fair. If the fight is fair, you've already made two mistakes, and you're already gone.

*Class Discipline (L1):* Stealth (1) + Sleight (1)

*Signature, Vanish:* As a maneuver, you may attempt to disappear from sight. Make a Stealth check. On a Standard or better result, you become invisible until the end of your next turn or until you attack. On Weak, you gain concealment instead (attacks against you have Bane). This is not magic; this is being very good at not being noticed.

*Secondary, Shadow Stride:* See the Shadow ability table below.

*Favored Skills:* Stealth, Deception, Sleight of Hand, Thievery, Acrobatics, Perception

*Starting Kit:* Two daggers, 6 throwing daggers, leather armor (DR 2), thieves' tools, disguise kit, 50 ft silk rope, grappling hook, smoke bomb (1, creates 10-ft radius heavy concealment for 1 round), 15 sp.

*Discipline Costs (Rank 1 / Rank 2 / Rank 3):*

#callout(type: "note", title: "The Stealth Economy", body: [
The Shadow doesn't trade blows. The Shadow's entire game is about controlling who can see them and who can't. Your turn is spend Maneuver to Vanish, move into position behind the enemy caster, then on your next turn, strike from invisibility with a Boon. If things go wrong, you have getaway tools: caltrops, smoke bombs, a disguise kit, and a network of contacts who owe you favors.

Your damage doesn't come from brute force. It comes from never being where the enemy is looking. When the Blade needs three rounds to carve through a knight's armor, the Shadow needs one round, one lockpick, and the knight's potion of healing quietly removed from his belt while he was too busy watching the Protector. You win by making the fight unfair. And you make it unfair before anyone knows you're there.
])

== Class Archetypes
#label("sec-class-archetypes")

The nine classes cluster into four archetypes, each with its own flavor and its own pool of class abilities. These aren't subclasses, they're families. A Protector and an Unbalanced feel different at the table, but they both solve problems with force. An Arcanist and an Intellect feel different, but they both solve problems with knowledge.

#figure(
  align(center)[#table(
    columns: (42.31%, 34.62%, 23.08%),
    align: (auto, auto, auto,),
    table.header([Archetype], [Classes], [Vibe]),
    [*Mage*], [Arcanist, Intellect], [Power through knowledge. Spells, wards, the right word at the right time.],
    [*Priest*], [Shepherd, Leader], [Power through faith. Healing, protection, inspiration.],
    [*Thief*], [Blade, Shadow], [Power through precision. Damage, infiltration, the unseen strike.],
    [*Fighter*], [Protector, Unbalanced], [Power through force. Defense, chaos, standing in the gap.],
  )],
  kind: table,
  outlined: false,
  numbering: none,
)

The *Odd* occupies no archetype. It is the pure wildcard, its abilities sampling all four archetype flavors. The Odd is the exception that proves the four-way rule. It doesn't fit. It's not supposed to.

#pagebreak()

== Class Abilities
#label("sec-class-abilities")

Every class has a list of abilities unique to it. These are the moves, spells, and tricks that define a hero's identity in play. Abilities are purchased using the flat card cost described in the Costs section below. Their real gate is Discipline prerequisites and level (Adept at 3, Master at 7). Every damaging ability is keyed to the damage budget table in @sec-damage-budget The abilities presented here define the class. Future supplements may expand them.

=== Odd Abilities

The Odd's abilities are few but strange: Improvised Solution, Wrong Context, Everything At Once. More emerge as the Odd experiments. They ignore Discipline prerequisites for their two free spells from *Eccentric Spellcasting*, but their Odd class abilities still require Disciplines.

    [*Wrong Number*], [Novice], [No prereq], [When you roll 3d6], [Flip one die to its opposite face, so 1 becomes 6 and 6 becomes 1. Once per scene.],

#pagebreak()

== Progression

You gain Development Points each level (see @sec-chapter-advancement for the full progression). Unspent DP carries over to your next level, so saving toward an 8 DP Master card is a real strategy.

*Adept* abilities unlock at Level 3. *Master* abilities unlock at Level 7. Until then, everything you buy is Novice.

#pagebreak()

== Costs

Your class determines how expensive each Discipline rank is to purchase. Cards (abilities, spells, skills) have a flat DP cost regardless of class: Novice 2 DP, Adept 4 DP, Master 8 DP. The total cost of a card = its flat card price + the sum of the discipline rank costs for each required discipline.

There are four cost structures, showing the price for rank 1 / rank 2 / rank 3:

#figure(
  align(center)[#table(
    columns: (25%, 18.18%, 18.18%, 18.18%, 20.45%),
    align: (auto, auto, auto, auto, auto,),
    table.header([Structure], [Rank 1], [Rank 2], [Rank 3], [Meaning]),
    [*Home*], [1 DP], [2 DP], [4 DP], [Favored: core to the class identity],
    [*Adjacent*], [2 DP], [4 DP], [8 DP], [Related but not core],
    [*Foreign*], [3 DP], [6 DP], [12 DP], [Unrelated to the class],
    [*Opposed*], [4 DP], [8 DP], [16 DP], [Out of class: antithetical to the class],
  )],
  kind: table,
  outlined: false,
  numbering: none,
)
